The A&P Lab/Build Module From Definition editor tool consumes this to generate the LabelSet, LearnSequence, PracticalTask, and QuizData for Module_Skeletal. Sources: OpenStax A&P 2e 7.2 'The Skull' (CC BY 4.0) and the author's Skull Labels.docx. Label anchorName values are matched to child meshes of the exploding-skull model via meshNameHints. The Explore info panels show: definition (left), pronunciation + landmarks + related (right).
title: Skeletal System: Skull & Bones
attribution: Adapted from OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e, Section 7.2 (CC BY 4.0). Access for free at openstax.org.

labels.definition: Forms the forehead and the roofs of the orbits (eye sockets). Contains the air-filled frontal sinus.
Paired bones forming most of the roof and upper sides of the cranium. They meet each other at the sagittal suture.
Form the lower sides and part of the base of the cranium. House the middle and inner ear and the jaw-joint socket (TMJ).
Forms the back and base of the skull. Its foramen magnum is where the spinal cord joins the brainstem.
Butterfly-shaped keystone of the skull base, touching every other cranial bone. Its sella turcica holds the pituitary gland.
Delicate bone between the eyes forming the nasal roof and upper septum. Its cribriform plate passes the smell (olfactory) nerves.
The paired maxillae form the upper jaw, holding the upper teeth and forming the front of the hard palate.
The cheekbones. Each forms the cheek prominence and part of the orbit, and helps form the zygomatic arch.
Two small bones that join at the midline to form the bridge of the nose and anchor the nasal cartilages.
The smallest facial bones, in the medial wall of each orbit. They help form the canal that drains tears into the nose.
Paired bones forming the back of the hard palate and part of the nasal wall, separating the mouth and nasal cavity.
Paired scroll-like bones on the lateral nasal walls that warm, moisten, and filter the air you breathe in.
A slender midline bone forming the lower part of the nasal septum, dividing the nasal cavity in two.
The lower jaw — the only moveable skull bone. It holds the lower teeth and hinges at the temporal bones (TMJ).

keyTerms.definition: The portion of the skull that encloses and protects the brain (8 brain-case bones).
An immobile fibrous joint between adjacent skull bones (coronal, sagittal, lambdoid, squamous).
Large opening in the occipital bone through which the spinal cord exits the skull.
Saddle-shaped depression of the sphenoid bone that houses the pituitary gland.
Air-filled cavities (frontal, maxillary, sphenoid, ethmoid) that lighten the skull and warm/moisten air.
Weakest point of the skull where four bones meet at the temple; overlies the middle meningeal artery.

steps.prompt: The skull has 22 bones: 8 in the brain case and 14 facial bones. Let's tour the brain case first.
Tap each glowing bone to reveal its name and role. Explode the skull to separate the bones.
Find the foramen magnum on the occipital bone — the spinal cord passes through here.
The sphenoid is the keystone bone that touches every other cranial bone. Its sella turcica holds the pituitary.
Quick check: which bones contain paranasal sinuses?

steps.instruction: Select the ONLY moveable bone of the skull.
steps.hint: It forms the lower jaw and moves at the TMJ.

steps.instruction: Select the bone that contains the foramen magnum.
steps.hint: It's at the back and base of the skull.

steps.instruction: Select the butterfly-shaped keystone bone at the central skull base.
steps.hint: It cradles the pituitary gland in the sella turcica.
It forms the lateral cheek and part of the orbit.

steps.instruction: Select the bone that forms the forehead.
Select the bone that houses the middle and inner ear.
steps.hint: It also forms the socket of the jaw joint (TMJ).

steps.instruction: Select the bone that forms the bridge of the nose.
steps.hint: Two small bones meet at the midline.

steps.instruction: Select the paired bone that forms the roof and upper sides of the cranium.
steps.hint: The pair meets at the sagittal suture.

steps.instruction: Select the upper jaw, which holds the upper teeth.
steps.hint: It also forms the anterior hard palate.

steps.instruction: Select the bone that forms the posterior part of the hard palate.
steps.hint: It sits behind the maxilla, between the oral and nasal cavities.

steps.instruction: Reassemble the skull: place the mandible into its socket on the skull.
steps.hint: It hinges at the temporal bones.
